M3CoT: A Novel Benchmark for Multi-Domain Multi-step Multi-modal Chain-of-Thought
confounds.detail: Models may reach correct answers via spurious shortcuts; intermediate steps may be wrong.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Assess step alignment/quality (e.g., CHAINEVAL, ROSCOE) alongside final accuracy and analyze gaps.

confounds.name: Infrastructure/API errors or parsing/extraction mistakes drive results

confounds.detail: Request failures or brittle extractors can mis-score outputs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Retry failed calls; robust regex/LLM fallback for extraction; manual verification on disputes; report unparseable rates and handling rules.

confounds.name: Scale/architecture, not the method, causes improvements
evidence: Chain-of-Thought Hub: A Continuous Effort to Measure Large Language Models' Reasoning Performance
Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
EffiReason-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models
confounds.detail: Larger or different backbones may dominate method comparisons.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Sweep sizes and families under matched settings and show method deltas persist; compare base vs SFT/RLHF variants.

confounds.name: Dataset contamination / memorization inflating scores

confounds.detail: Benchmarks or solutions seen during training/finetuning can artifactually raise performance and apparent method gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate on contamination-reduced variants (e.g., GSM8K-Hard) or recent/held-out compositions; analyze temporal saturation and report persistence of gains.

confounds.name: Heterogeneous reporting / benchmark adoption bias
evidence: Chain-of-Thought Hub: A Continuous Effort to Measure Large Language Models' Reasoning Performance
The Ouroboros of Benchmarking: Reasoning Evaluation in an Era of Saturation
confounds.detail: Cross-family comparisons may be skewed by selective reporting and evolving benchmark sets.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Aggregate official reports, analyze adoption overlap and trends, and caution comparisons; wherever possible, re-run under unified protocols.

confounds.name: Multiple comparisons / inappropriate statistical tests
evidence: The Benefits of a Concise Chain of Thought on Problem-Solving in Large Language Models
To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
confounds.detail: Spurious significance from many tests or violated assumptions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Apply paired bootstrapping with correction or non-parametric tests after normality checks; report corrected p-values.

confounds.name: Tool/scaffolding use, not internal reasoning, explains success/failure
evidence: LongCoT: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
M3CoT: A Novel Benchmark for Multi-Domain Multi-step Multi-modal Chain-of-Thought
confounds.detail: External tools or agentic scaffolds may dominate outcomes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Primary evaluations disallow tools; include ablations comparing reasoning-only vs tool-enabled modes and attribute domain-specific effects.

confounds.name: World-knowledge retrieval, not reasoning, drives gains
evidence: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
confounds.detail: Tasks with factual priors may be solved via recall.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Per-task analyses showing where CoT helps/harms and focusing on math/symbolic slices; split mixed benchmarks by math-like indicators (e.g., ‘=’) to localize effects.

confounds.name: Context-window/output budget limits cause failures
evidence: LongCoT: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
confounds.detail: Long chains may fail due to token limits, not reasoning deficits.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Allow large output budgets, measure tokens used, and study accuracy vs chain/DAG size against independent-error baselines.

confounds.name: Efficiency metrics bias the trade-off
evidence: EffiReason-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models
confounds.detail: Prior metrics can create discontinuities or over-weight token savings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use a smooth CES-inspired E3-Score with documented sensitivity and report Accuracy/Tokens/E3 jointly.

confounds.name: Evaluation mismatch for free-form outputs
evidence: To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
confounds.detail: String match may mark correct paraphrases as wrong.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use LLM judges or tolerant matching and report judged metrics in addition to exact match.

confounds.name: Exemplar surface patterns, not reasoning, drive few-shot gains
evidence: EffiReason-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models
confounds.detail: Formatting or lexical cues may be exploited instead of structure.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Noise-injection into exemplars and cross-domain transfers to probe robustness to surface changes.

confounds.name: Human baselines are noisy or unrepresentative
evidence: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
confounds.detail: Claims of surpassing humans may hinge on unstable human scores.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare to both average and maximum human scores and qualify interpretation.

confounds.name: Prompt-content differences (instructions/options/examples) explain gains
evidence: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
confounds.detail: Improvements attributed to CoT could instead come from stronger prompts with instructions and options.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run answer-only baselines with the same instructions/options/examples and show additional CoT gains beyond that baseline.

experiment_recipes.goal: Harness integrity on GSM8K with greedy decoding and robust extraction
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Zero-shot and few-shot direct vs CoT with fixed decoding and robust extraction — Evaluate both zero- and few-shot; greedy decoding; per-dataset tailored answer extractors; treat unparseable outputs per protocol.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On a random 200-item subset of the GSM8K test split with temperature=0 (greedy): (i) unparseable-plan rate <= 2.0% for both Direct and CoT runs; (ii) regex-based final-answer extraction succeeds on >= 98.0% of attempted items; (iii) a random-guess baseline attains Accuracy <= 1.0%. Any violation refutes.
constraints_not_enforced: Manual verification by humans of disputed extractions
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies core evaluation hygiene (fixed decoding, robust extraction, baseline sanity) before running costlier headline tests.

experiment_recipes.goal: GSM8K CoT vs Direct under standard protocol with significance and efficiency metrics
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Few-shot Chain-of-Thought as standard setup; final-answer scoring — Use few-shot CoT across models, score only final answers; use reported numbers when available and mark re-runs separately.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Evaluate both Direct-answer and few-shot CoT with identical instructions/options/examples except the CoT instruction, using temperature=0. Attempt coverage >= 95.0% of the test split for both methods; 95% paired bootstrap CI half-width for Accuracy <= 3.0 percentage points for both methods; and Holm–Bonferroni–corrected paired-bootstrapped p-values are computed and reported for Direct vs CoT. Any unmet criterion refutes.
constraints_not_enforced: LLM judging for free-form equivalence not used (strict/flexible regex only)
depends_on: Harness integrity on GSM8K with greedy decoding and robust extraction
experiment_recipes.rationale: Implements the field-standard Direct vs CoT comparison with fixed decoding, final-answer scoring, and significance plus efficiency reporting on a canonical math benchmark.

experiment_recipes.goal: BBH multi-task CoT vs Direct with corrected significance and coverage
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Zero-shot and few-shot direct vs CoT with fixed decoding and robust extraction — Evaluate both zero- and few-shot; greedy decoding; per-dataset tailored answer extractors; treat unparseable outputs per protocol.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Run Direct vs CoT on >= 10 distinct BBH tasks with temperature=0; for each task, attempt coverage >= 95.0% and 95% bootstrap CI half-width for task Accuracy <= 5.0 percentage points; across tasks, compute Holm–Bonferroni–corrected paired-bootstrapped p-values. All conditions must hold; otherwise refute.
constraints_not_enforced: Tool usage is disallowed but explicit tool-ablation not performed here
depends_on: Harness integrity on GSM8K with greedy decoding and robust extraction
experiment_recipes.rationale: Checks standard-practice Direct vs CoT evaluation and significance on a long-horizon, multi-task reasoning suite to avoid single-benchmark artifacts.

experiment_recipes.goal: CoT vs CCoT vs Direct at matched token budgets on GSM8K
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: CoT prompt variants (e.g., CCoT/Desp-CoT/CCoT) vs standard CoT — Match task and exemplars while varying CoT verbosity/wording.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using the same items, instructions, options, and exemplars, run Direct, CCoT, and standard CoT with temperature=0 and enforce matched average output tokens such that the methods’ average tokens differ by <= 10.0% pairwise. Also compute Holm–Bonferroni–corrected paired-bootstrapped p-values between all pairs. Both the token-matching and corrected p-value computations must succeed; otherwise refute.
depends_on: GSM8K CoT vs Direct under standard protocol with significance and efficiency metrics
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ablates verbosity to attribute gains to the reasoning strategy rather than longer outputs, a core norm for CoT-style claims.

experiment_recipes.goal: Robustness via contamination-resistant split GSM8K-Hard and effect persistence
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Zero-shot and few-shot direct vs CoT with fixed decoding and robust extraction — Evaluate both zero- and few-shot; greedy decoding; per-dataset tailored answer extractors; treat unparseable outputs per protocol.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: With temperature=0 and identical prompts/exemplars as in GSM8K, evaluate Direct and CoT on GSM8K-Hard with attempt coverage >= 95.0%. Let Δ_clean be (CoT−Direct) Accuracy on GSM8K from the headline recipe and Δ_hard the same on GSM8K-Hard; require Δ_hard >= 0.50 × Δ_clean and both 95% CIs computed. Otherwise refute robustness of the observed effect.
constraints_not_enforced: LLM judging for free-form answers not used
Human verification of necessity of perturbations not conducted
depends_on: GSM8K CoT vs Direct under standard protocol with significance and efficiency metrics
experiment_recipes.rationale: Guards against contamination/memorization by testing whether Direct vs CoT effects persist on a robustness-targeted split.

experiment_recipes.goal: Sampling budget sweep to separate brute-force from reasoning on GSM8K
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Efficiency benchmarking with fixed exemplars and E3-Score — Fix exemplar lists once with a global seed; run k∈{1,4,8,12}; cross-domain transfers and noise-injected exemplars; report Accuracy/Tokens/E3.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: With fixed exemplars (global seed) and temperature=0, produce Pass@k and Consistency@k for k in {1,4,8,12} on the same item set, with 95% bootstrap CIs for each k and method. All four k settings must be successfully computed for both Direct and CoT; otherwise refute.
constraints_not_enforced: Compute-equalization across methods beyond k control not enforced
depends_on: Harness integrity on GSM8K with greedy decoding and robust extraction
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ensures reported gains are not purely due to increased sampling attempts, a standard control in reasoning evaluations.
